verdict.rationale: Asana's own docs name a native Rules feature: developers can build "rule actions" and app components "on the surface of tasks or rules", AI Studio is billed as "powerful no-code automations", and a directory listing shows Rules automatically creating PagerDuty incidents from tasks. The evidence never documents the event-trigger/condition/action model itself, so only the depth of the capability is unproven. Webhooks and third-party tools like Zapier are adjacent and earn no credit. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of rule triggers, events, conditions and available actions, plus independent or hands-on corroboration of rule-based automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Automate tedious work in powerful, bespoke ways with our platform features like rule actions, webhooks, and our API.
Build app components on the surface of tasks or rules so that customers can use their favorite tools and stay in flow.
Automatically create PagerDuty incidents with context from Asana tasks using Rules.
